definition: A cognitive distortion is a maladaptive pattern of thinking that can shape how a person interprets situations and relationships. In this packet, interpersonal cognitive distortions include tendencies such as expecting rejection or having unrealistic relationship expectations, which may contribute to avoidance and other coping problems.

reasons: The definition’s first sentence (“maladaptive pattern of thinking” and that it “can shape how a person interprets situations and relationships”) is not explicitly supported in the packet text.

The packet discusses *interpersonal cognitive distortions (ICDs)* and identifies dimensions including “interpersonal rejection” and “unrealistic relationship expectations,” but it does not provide enough support for the general framing in the first sentence.
The packet supports interpersonal cognitive distortions, not a general definition of "cognitive distortion" as such; the broader opening claim is unsupported by the source.
"Can shape how a person interprets situations and relationships" is an unsupported generalization beyond the packet.

The mention of "avoidance and other coping problems" overreaches the packet, which only suggests avoidance of social discomfort, digital reassurance seeking, and problematic smartphone use/nomophobia.
